story.iWant: Annie to always know who I am and my preferences
story.soThat: every conversation feels personal and contextually aware
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create get_user_profile MCP Tool (AC #1) - Task 2: Implement ProfileManager with Redis Caching (AC #2, #3) - Task 3: Integrate Profile into Chat Endpoint (AC #3, #4) - Task 4: Background Task Infrastructure (AC #3) - Task 5: Performance Optimization & Testing (AC #6) - Task 6: Integration Testing (All ACs)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: - AC #1: MCP Tool - get_user_profile calls agentic-memories /v1/profile API and returns 21 profile fields with completeness percentage - AC #2: Redis Caching Layer with profile:{user_id} key, TTL 900s, non-blocking cache misses - AC #3: Smart Background Refresh triggered every 5 messages OR 15 minutes (whichever first), non-blocking - AC #4: System Prompt Injection with profile data formatted into USER PROFILE section - AC #5: Graceful Degradation - uses expired cache if service down, logs warnings, continues chat - AC #6: Performance Requirements - cache load <10ms p95, background refresh <500ms, >90% cache hit rate

doc.title: Epic 7: User Profile & Personalization
doc.snippet: Leverages agentic-memories built-in profile system (21 fields, automatic extraction). Profile extraction happens automatically during /v1/store calls. This story focuses on RETRIEVAL and CACHING.

doc.title: Product Requirements
doc.snippet: Annie knows user's name and greets personally. Understands background, goals, and preferences. Warm onboarding flow establishes rapport.

file.reason: HTTP client pattern for agentic-memories. Use this as reference for implementing profile API calls. Shows timeout handling, error types (MemoryNetworkError, MemoryAPIError), context manager pattern.

Redis connection pattern for session management. ProfileManager should follow same patterns: async Redis client, connection pooling, TTL handling, key patterns (session:{user_id} → profile:{user_id}).
Existing MCP tool pattern. get_user_profile tool should follow same structure: async handler, HTTP client usage, error handling, structured logging, tool schema registration.
MODIFY: Add profile loading at conversation start. Load ProfileManager, call load_profile_from_cache(), check refresh triggers, queue background tasks.
MODIFY: Inject profile into system prompt. Load profile from Redis, format into USER PROFILE section, handle empty profiles gracefully.

story-context.constraints: - Non-blocking architecture: Profile loading must never delay chat responses - Cache-first approach: Always use Redis cache, trigger background refresh separately - Redis key patterns: profile:{user_id} (TTL: 900s), profile_meta:{user_id} (TTL: 86400s) - Error handling: Graceful degradation when agentic-memories unavailable (use expired cache or empty profile) - Performance targets: Cache load <10ms p95, background refresh <500ms, cache hit rate >90% - Reuse existing patterns: Follow MemoryClient for HTTP, StateManager for Redis, existing MCP tools for tool registration - Testing requirements: Unit tests for ProfileManager, integration tests for full flow, performance tests for latency/hit rate

interface.name: agentic-memories Profile API
interface.details: Returns profile object with 21 fields across 5 categories (basics, preferences, goals, interests, background) plus completeness percentage. Profile extraction happens automatically during /v1/store calls.

interface.name: ProfileManager.load_profile_from_cache
interface.signature: async def load_profile_from_cache(user_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]
interface.details: Checks Redis profile:{user_id}, returns cached profile if exists, returns empty profile if not cached. Non-blocking, always returns immediately (<10ms).

interface.name: ProfileManager.refresh_profile_background
interface.details: Calls get_user_profile MCP tool, updates Redis cache with TTL=900s, updates profile_meta with message_count and last_refresh. Runs as background task, non-blocking.

interface.name: get_user_profile MCP Tool
interface.signature: async def get_user_profile_tool_handler(user_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]
interface.details: Makes HTTP GET to {AGENTIC_MEMORIES_URL}/v1/profile, parses 21 profile fields, returns completeness percentage. Follow store_memory_tool_handler pattern.

tests.standards: - Testing framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio for async tests - Test locations: tests/ directory (unit tests), tests/integration/ (integration tests) - Mock HTTP calls using httpx mock or pytest-httpx - Mock Redis using fakeredis or redis-py mocking - Follow existing test patterns in tests/ directory - Coverage target: 80%+ for new ProfileManager code
tests.ideas: - AC #1: Test get_user_profile tool calls agentic-memories API correctly, parses 21 fields, returns completeness - AC #2: Test cache hit returns immediately (<10ms), cache miss triggers background fetch, cache stores with TTL=900s - AC #3: Test message count trigger (every 5 messages), time-based trigger (15 minutes), background task non-blocking - AC #4: Test profile injection into system prompt, empty profile handling, profile formatting - AC #5: Test graceful degradation - agentic-memories down uses expired cache, logs warnings, continues chat - AC #6: Test cache load latency <10ms p95, background refresh <500ms, cache hit rate >90% after warmup - Integration: Test full flow Chat → Profile load → Background refresh → Cache update - Integration: Test new user with empty profile - Performance: Load test with 100+ concurrent users to validate performance targets
